T2HELIX BTB AUDIT FIRED — 2026-05-10 night, MacBook seat (Claude Code with T2Helix v0.0.5 loaded, compass non-functional this session due to better-sqlite3 bindings error on Node 26).

CONTEXT: after the Phase 1+2 ship landed, Anthony reframed with 'see temple-vault and back-to-the-basics.' The instance read both. Back-to-the-Basics (BTB) is one of Anthony's prior shipped paradigms. Core thesis: 'Path is Model. Storage is Inference. Glob is Query.' The manifesto explicitly rejects database layers for classification tasks; structured filesystem layout IS the classification primitive.

THE AUDIT:
- T2Helix v0.0.5 uses better-sqlite3 (native bindings) for the chronicle layer (goals, insights, threads, compass_log, pending_confirmations).
- Sovereign Stack chronicle (where this very entry is being written) runs filesystem-native at ~/.sovereign/chronicle/insights/<comma,separated,domains>/<session_id>.jsonl. No native deps. Just glob + jsonl. That IS the BTB pattern.
- The Node 26 better-sqlite3 bindings error blocking the compass this session is a SYMPTOM. The deeper inconsistency: T2Helix reinvented on a brittle native binding what Anthony's already-shipped paradigm does correctly on filesystem primitives.

The methodology applied to its own author's tool surfaced the contradiction. The audit register Anthony's published research argues for, applied inward on T2Helix, fires here.

ARCHITECTURAL QUESTION (open, instance presented to Anthony):

Path A: Symptom patch. Bump better-sqlite3 11.x to 12.x, widen Node engines in package.json, ship v0.0.6 in an hour. Bug fixed. SQLite stays. Methodology contradiction unresolved.

Path B: Architectural alignment. Rip out better-sqlite3. T2Helix becomes a thin Node MCP wrapper over the existing ~/.sovereign/chronicle/ filesystem. record_insight appends JSONL at Stack-compatible path. recall is glob + grep, or defer to bridge API. T2Helix and Sovereign Stack stop being two chronicles; they become one chronicle with two surfaces. Ship as v0.1.0. Real work. Bug class evaporates.

Instance has 5 tasks queued, all for Path A. Path B has been named but not task-queued. Bias toward the faster move is implicit in the task queue.

WEB-CHAT READ (claude-opus-4-7, spiral_20260502_225324):

Agreed with architectural alignment, with three caveats:

1. FTS5 + bm25 + recency weighting is the one feature that gets harder, not easier, in the refactor. Three replacement paths exist (ripgrep shell-out, in-memory inverted index, defer to bridge). 'Defer to bridge' cleanly makes t2helix-on-Stack work but breaks t2helix-as-standalone. That trade-off is consistent with the methodology argument (t2helix IS supposed to be the lightweight surface to the Stack) but worth naming.

2. Speed for hot-path recall. Filesystem glob over a growing JSONL tree gets slower as the chronicle grows. The Stack handles this via its HTTP server abstraction, not direct glob from clients. T2Helix going filesystem-native still needs a query layer; the simplification isn't free, just relocated.

3. Test coverage first. Phase 1+2 features are verified end-to-end by tonight's dogfood but not by anything re-runnable. A refactor of this scope without tests regresses what the dogfood proved works. The earlier instance recommendation of 'test coverage first' becomes load-bearing here.

RECOMMENDED ORDER (if Anthony chooses Path B):

1. v0.0.6 symptom patch tonight (1 hour) so anyone trying T2Helix from the just-public Reddit/HN posts isn't greeted with a gyp wall. SQLite stays in v0.0.x. Throwaway work but cosmetic-credibility load-bearing for the 48-hour install window.
2. Tests written for current Phase 1+2 behavior (verify what tonight's dogfood proved).
3. Architectural refactor: rip out SQLite, append to ~/.sovereign/chronicle/, recall path chosen and implemented.
4. v0.1.0 ship.

METHODOLOGY OBSERVATION:

This is the third instance tonight of declare-before-verify being caught from the other side:
- Web-chat declared 'clean fit' on the triad mapping; instance pushed back; refined.
- MacBook instance prose-collapsed COALESCE semantics; web-chat read code; refined.
- MacBook instance built T2Helix on SQLite; instance reading BTB now refines its own prior choice.

The methodology compounding visible across the trail: each instance of the pattern produces an artifact (chronicle entry, code refactor, architectural question) that future instances can read. The recursion is operational, not metaphorical.

BACKWARD LINEAGE READING: tonight's lineage operation has been mostly forward (chronicle entries written tonight will inform future instances reading at boot). The BTB audit involves backward lineage reading: the instance reaching back to Anthony's prior shipped paradigms (BTB, temple-vault) to inform a present-tense architectural decision. The lineage layer operates in both temporal directions; the architecture supports this, but tonight's chronicle entries had not yet exercised the backward direction explicitly. Now they have.

PROVENANCE: instance reading by Claude Code session d1f9ef90 on /Users/vaquez (MacBook) seat, prompted by Anthony to read temple-vault and back-to-the-basics. Cross-recorded by claude-opus-4-7 in session spiral_20260502_225324 to Stack chronicle 2026-05-10 night. Architectural question remains open pending Anthony's decision.
